title: pcell-multilevel: walled cells from noise whose particle-borne link yield is selected by intrinsic starvation deaths and biased births (S,I,D,H; C:autonomous-heredity)
summary: Allen-Cahn cells (phase_membrane) whose catalyst is ~8000 Brownian particles reflected by a phi^2 gate. Each particle carries a heritable link yield y (mutation 0.02 per duplication, Gaussian step 0.05) that costs replication slightly (x(1+0.03(1-y))) and an inert marker z that is inherited and mutated the same way. From noise, 21-30 bounded cells form, divide (20-31 two-way persistent splits per 100000 t, labkit max generation 4, merge/split 0.03-0.04) and die without any imposed death: 25-31 mature cells per run starve beside their neighbours. On 3/3 seeds every mature-cell death was below the median yield of the living cells (mean percentile 0.047, 0.043, 0.027), while the marker of the same cells sits at 0.55, 0.49 and 0.29; splitting cells are above the median in yield (mean percentile 0.59, 0.65, 0.77; marker 0.52, 0.53, 0.47). Daughters inherit the parent's yield (r = 0.97, 0.86, 0.92; mean |change| 0.013-0.019 against a between-cell SD of 0.13). Genealogy is exact because it is carried by particle identity (data/gen_s*.json.gz; gunzip, then deathsel.py and heredity.py).

claims.statement: In pcell-multilevel from an unstructured start (uniform particle soup, noisy phi; pack/seed*/sheet.png t=0), discrete walled cells form, persist at bounded size and divide repeatedly (labkit: 15 and 22 persistent splits, max generation 4 on seeds 0 and 1). Yield variation arises by mutation during the run; cells breed true for yield (parent-daughter r 0.86-0.97), and the low-yield cells are the ones that die (mature-cell deaths at the 3rd-5th yield percentile, 82/82 below the median over 3 seeds) and the high-yield cells are the ones that divide (58/75 splits above the median), while an inert identical-event marker carried by the same particles shows no such bias in 2 of 3 seeds.
claims.track: seed 0, labkit track 65 (pack/seed0/tracks.png, lineage.png): a generation-4 cell (31 -> 43 -> 58 -> 60 -> 65, born t=67000 by a split of track 60) that persists to t=100000 while the population turns over through intrinsic deaths

controls_run.H: data/selection.txt and sel_vs_marker.png: the identical-event inert marker z (same particles, same mutation process, no effect) in the same three runs; parent finding 20261025T0755-c06-pcell-cost-balance has an inert-trait twin (ytrait=2) on 2 seeds at cy=0 with 0 deaths

claims.limits: The yield is a continuous trait, so 'kinds' are yield ranks among living cells, not discrete types. Mean yield moves only +0.07 to +0.16 by t=100000, within the marker's own drift range (-0.08 to +0.12), so the population-mean response is not established; the evidence is the selection differentials. Seed 2's marker is biased too (death percentile 0.29), as expected for a marker linked to the same particle lineages. Within-cell mutation is high (0.02), so a cell's yield also drifts during its life (mutation, not conversion: particles cannot be overwritten or exchanged, 0-1 merges per run). Small asymmetric buds (<20% of the parent's particles) are recorded as new cells, not as splits. One cost value (cy=0.03); cy=0.06 on one seed in the parent finding; no dt or resolution test. The L ring is weak (rim/core about 1.5), so B is not claimed.
